user_stories.story: As a user, I see DailyLog as an X-inspired single-column feed (sticky header, divided posts, pill buttons) in light or dark per my OS setting.
As a pointer user, I get hover feedback; as a touch or keyboard user I lose nothing because controls look like controls at rest.
As a keyboard user, I can Tab to every control in logical order and always see where focus is.
As any user, I get instant pressed feedback when I click or tap a button.
As an editor, I can see which photos are marked for removal, without relying on color.
As a user, I can tell when a save or delete is in progress (distinct from a disabled control), and the original label returns afterwards.
As a user, when something fails I am told what failed and what to do next, with the server detail still visible.
As a phone user at 360px, I never need to scroll horizontally.

acceptance_criteria.c: Only frontend/style.css and frontend/app.js change (index.html only if strictly necessary, with the reason recorded). No new files, no external fonts, libraries, CDNs or @import url. Backend untouched; the 112 backend tests pass. The real logs.db and uploads/ are never touched (verification uses temp paths). Pass: file diff and test run.

style.css is non-empty and defines colors as CSS custom properties on :root, with a prefers-color-scheme: dark override. Computed body background differs between emulated light and dark. Font-family is a system stack. Pass: computed styles in both emulations.

Content column max-width is about 600px and centered at a 1280px viewport. The header is position: sticky at top: 0 with an opaque or near-opaque background and stays at the top after scrolling. Posts (li.log) are separated by a thin border. Pass: computed styles and bounding rects.

#save-button and .edit-save-button are pill-shaped (border-radius at least half of height), X-blue background (about #1d9bf0), with white or dark text meeting 4.5:1. .edit-button and .edit-cancel-button are neutral outline pills. .delete-button is red-themed (text or border red, 4.5:1 text). At rest each button has a visible fill or border distinguishing it from plain text. Pass: computed background, border and radius.

.log-photos is a grid or flex layout with rounded-corner images (border-radius at least 8px), images constrained to the container (max-width 100%, no overflow). In .edit-form the .edit-photo items show image, checkbox and "Remove" text legibly. Pass: computed styles and screenshots.
.log-date uses a muted color distinct from body text and has at least 4.5:1 contrast against its background in both themes. Pass: contrast computed from computed colors.

All visible text (labels, h1, h2, description, buttons, date, empty message, error text, placeholder if any) has at least 4.5:1 contrast against its effective background in light and dark. Pass: script computes ratios from computed color and background.

Every :hover rule is inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). Hovering a button with a real mouse changes some computed property (background, border or filter) versus rest. With hover not emulated, no :hover rule applies. Pass: stylesheet inspection (no :hover outside that media block) and computed-style comparison.

Every interactive element (#description, #photos, #save-button, .edit-button, .delete-button, edit textarea, edit file input, remove checkboxes, .edit-save-button, .edit-cancel-button) shows a :focus-visible outline of at least 2px, with outline-offset such that it is not clipped (not hidden by overflow or the sticky header), and at least 3:1 contrast against both the adjacent background and the element's own fill, in light and dark. Focus is never removed (no outline: none without a replacement). Scrolling a focused element into view is not covered by the sticky header (scroll-padding-top or scroll-margin is at least header height). Pass: computed outline color/width plus contrast, and screenshots.

Tab order on the initial page: #description, #photos, #save-button, then each post's Edit, Delete in DOM order. In edit mode: textarea, each Remove checkbox in photo order, Add photos input, Save, Cancel. Verified by real Tab key presses via CDP and activeElement ids and classes. No tabindex above 0 and no focusable element hidden by CSS.
Every button, file input, textarea and checkbox (or its label hit area) has a bounding box of at least 24x24 CSS px, at 1280px and at 360px. Pass: getBoundingClientRect.

Each button has an :active style (for example darker background or transform: scale below 1) that differs from rest and hover. There is no transition delay on :active (transition-duration at most 100ms or none for the pressed state). Pass: dispatch mousePressed via CDP and read computed style while held.

In the edit form, a .edit-photo whose checkbox is checked differs from an unchecked one by at least two cues, one of them not color: dimmed image (opacity below 1), a visible outline or border (red) and/or a visible text state (for example the label text changes to "Will be removed" or shows a strikethrough or marker). Unchecking restores the rest appearance. Pass: check via a real click and compare computed styles and text.

While a request is in flight (intercepted via CDP Fetch), the acting button has aria-busy="true", is disabled (preventing double submit), and its text is an in-progress label: "Saving..." for #save-button and .edit-save-button, "Deleting..." for .delete-button. CSS renders a spinner or progress indicator on [aria-busy="true"] (pseudo-element with non-zero size or equivalent). It is visibly different from a plain disabled button: a disabled button without aria-busy has a different style (for example reduced opacity and not-allowed cursor), while a busy one keeps full text legibility at 4.5:1 or more. After the response (success or failure) aria-busy is removed and the original label is restored ("Save", "Save", "Delete"). Request logic, order and payloads are unchanged. Pass: screenshots during the intercept, attribute and text reads before, during and after.

With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce emulated, no infinite animation runs on the busy indicator (animation-name none or animation-iteration-count not infinite), yet a static indicator is still visible (for example a static ring or "..." marker). Transitions are removed or negligible. Without reduce, the indicator is animated. Pass: computed animation properties in both emulations.

No control is left disabled without a visible reason: any disabled state in the app is only the loading state of criterion 14, and the busy label itself states the reason. No other code path sets disabled without aria-busy. Pass: during intercept, every disabled button also has aria-busy="true" and an in-progress label; at rest none is disabled.

All error areas (#form-error, #load-error, .edit-error, .delete-error) when shown have a red-themed color or border and a non-color cue (an icon or text prefix such as a pseudo-element glyph or "Error:" text) so the state is recognizable in grayscale. Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 in both themes. They keep role="alert" and wrap long text without overflow. The [hidden] attribute still hides them (display none wins over any display rule). Pass: computed styles, ::before content, and screenshots.

Error messages are shaped as what failed plus what to do next, and keep the API detail visible. Save failure: "Couldn't save your log: invalid or corrupt image. Choose a JPG, PNG or WEBP photo and try again." Known detail strings map to a hint: "invalid or corrupt image" (choose a JPG, PNG or WEBP photo), "photo exceeds 5 MiB" (choose a smaller photo, under 5 MB), "a log needs between 1 and 5 photos" (keep between 1 and 5 photos), "log not found" (it may already be deleted; reload the page). Unknown detail or non-JSON gets the detail or status plus "Please try again." Network failure: "Couldn't save your log: could not reach the server. Check your connection and try again." Edit uses "Couldn't update your log: ...", delete uses "Couldn't delete your log: ...", load uses "Couldn't load your logs: ... Reload the page or try again later." Pass: intercepted responses (400/404/500/network failure) produce the expected text in each error area, with the API detail substring present.
Errors clear and hide at the start of the next attempt, as today. Pass: trigger an error, retry successfully, and the error area is hidden with empty text.

At 360px width (Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride), document.documentElement.scrollWidth is at most 360 in both themes, with the list populated with a long unbroken description string, multiple photos, and edit mode open. Textareas and file inputs fit within the container. Pass: scrollWidth check and 360px screenshots.

Existing behavior is preserved: create, edit (one at a time, Cancel restores the view), delete with confirm, empty message, ordering and the selectors and ids listed in the request. app.js uses no innerHTML with user or API data. Pass: end-to-end run against a temp-path server, plus grep for innerHTML.

Screenshots are captured for light, dark and 360px with a populated list, plus one each of: edit mode with a photo marked for removal, a busy button, an error shown, and a keyboard focus ring. Nothing is visibly broken (no overlap, clipped focus rings, or unreadable text). Pass: screenshots reviewed.

assumptions.a: "Easterned UX inspired by X" means an X (Twitter)-inspired look, per the orchestrator reading. Not a blocking ambiguity.
Loading state: in-flight buttons are both disabled and aria-busy="true"; this keeps double-submit protection while CSS distinguishes loading from plain disabled.

Busy labels are set via textContent and restored in finally blocks to the original text, with no change to request logic. The label may be changed in JS or via CSS only if the visible text still reads in-progress and aria-busy is set; JS text change is preferred.

Checkbox selected-state cue is done in CSS (:has(input:checked) or sibling selectors) with the "Remove" text state changed in CSS (pseudo-element) so app.js needs no change for it. If the implementer needs JS for the text, it is allowed as a loading/state label change only.
Photo alt text "Log photo" stays unchanged. Colors: primary around #1d9bf0 is adjustable to reach 4.5:1 for text, for example darker blue or dark text on it.
MiB vs MB: the hint says "under 5 MB" per the form label wording.
index.html needs no change (the stylesheet link already exists).

edge_cases.e: Very long unbroken description text or error text must wrap (overflow-wrap) without causing horizontal scroll at 360px.
[hidden] elements (#form-error, #empty-message, #load-error, hidden original post children in edit mode) stay hidden even when the CSS sets display on those selectors.
A post being deleted: error area appended to the li is shown below actions. After a failed delete the button returns to enabled with its "Delete" label.
After a successful save or delete, loadLogs re-renders the list; the busy state on a detached button must not leave stale state, and the #save-button is restored.
Native file input button ("Choose files") must also meet the focus and size criteria. Styling via ::file-selector-button is acceptable.
Forced-colors or high-contrast mode: focus ring and busy indicator should not vanish (use outline rather than box-shadow only).
Touch devices (hover: none): no hover rules apply and controls remain distinguishable.
Sticky header must not cover a focused field when tabbing or scrolling.
Edit mode with 5 photos and 360px width lays out without overflow.
Network failure (fetch rejects) and non-JSON error bodies get the generic fallback text with "Please try again."

risks.risk: Focus indicator contrast of 3:1 must hold against both the page background and the filled blue button in both themes; a single outline color may fail one, so use a two-tone (outline plus offset gap) ring and verify by computation.
Disabled buttons with a busy spinner: default disabled styling or low opacity can drop text below 4.5:1; busy style must keep legibility.
:has() support for the selected-photo styling; the headless Chrome version supports it, but fallback to a sibling structure may be needed.
Error hint mapping depends on exact backend detail strings; unknown strings fall back to the generic hint.
Changing the button label while busy could shift layout width; keep it stable (min-width) to avoid jumps.

dependencies.d: Headless Chrome at C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe with CDP; backend served from a temp DB and uploads path. No new packages.

spec.self_critique: Every story maps to criteria: X look (2-5), hover (8), tab and focus (9-11), pressed (12), selected (13), loading and disabled (14-16), errors (17-19), 360px (20). Each criterion is checkable by computed style, contrast math, Tab order, aria-busy under an intercept, or a screenshot. The biggest risk is the ambiguity of how strictly "X-inspired" is judged (subjective, covered only by criteria 3-5 and 22) and the dual-surface focus-ring contrast. The spec also assumes busy buttons are disabled and aria-busy together, which the brief implies but does not state outright.
